selected.title: Who checks the draft
selected.texas_link: UT Physicians is the clinical practice of McGovern Medical School at UTHealth Houston, and the University of Texas System announced access to the same kind of tool through its health AI initiative. The film draws a generic illustrated exam room and names no real clinic, clinician or patient.

movement.action: is working toward adopting Epic's ambient listening platform as one unified system after pilots of two other ambient AI products
movement.object: ambient AI that drafts clinical visit notes

selected.why_today: On October 8th, 2026 Abridge announced an enterprise agreement with University of Texas REAL Health AI, which adds a systemwide access framework to the UT Physicians plan that the school published on September 9th, 2026.
selected.consequence: A physician's note work moves from typing it afterward to checking a draft that software wrote while the visit happened.
selected.application_change: Clinic visit notes at UT health institutions can move from clinicians typing after the visit to AI drafting during it, with the clinician reviewing the draft.
selected.counter_image: No source here gives a switch date, an accuracy measure, time saved or a patient consent step. The Abridge figures are the vendor's own, and the school page doesn't say the Abridge agreement has been deployed.
selected.earned_take: The draft belongs to the doctor who signs it, and how well that check works isn't published.

agency.next_step: UT Physicians has no published switch or completion date, and each UT health institution decides its own use under the framework.
agency.who_can_act: UT Physicians and McGovern Medical School leadership, the leaders of each UT health institution, and the Texas Medical Board, which the statute names as the source of the records standard.

filmability.viewer_question: When an AI listens to a Texas doctor's visit and drafts the note, who checks it before it goes in the record?
filmability.opening_action: An illustrated exam room where a conversation becomes a draft line on a note screen, disclosed as Illustration.
filmability.mechanism: Input: the spoken visit. Transformation: software drafts the note and, per the vendor, links each line to source data. Result: the clinician reviews the draft, and Texas law conditions AI diagnostic use on practitioner review of all AI-created records. Limit: no source measures how well the check works.
filmability.human_consequence: Physicians at UT Physicians and other UT health institutions, whose documentation work becomes checking, and the patients whose words become the source of the record. No person is named and no outcome is claimed.
filmability.source_limit: The Abridge figures and design claims are the vendor's own. The school page gives no date, accuracy or time figure. The statute is written around diagnosis, and its text doesn't say whether a visit note counts. No footage of any Texas exam room exists in the sources.
